title: Consent, right of publicity and deepfake law

queue.claim: NO FAKES Act (S.1367/H.R.2794, reintroduced April 2025) was not enacted as of mid-2026. Its key terms: post-mortem right renewable up to 70 years, liability for products 'primarily designed' to make replicas of specific people, notice-and-takedown safe harbour, partial pre-emption of state law.

queue.claim: EU AI Act Art. 50 transparency obligations (machine-readable marking under 50(2), deepfake disclosure under 50(4)) apply from 2 August 2026. The Art. 2(12) open-source exemption does not cover Art. 50. The November 2025 Digital Omnibus proposed an Art. 50(2) grace period, and a code of practice on labelling AI-generated content was being drafted.

queue.claim: Tennessee ELVIS Act (signed 21 Mar 2024, effective 1 Jul 2024) creates liability for distributing an 'algorithm, software, tool, or other technology' whose primary purpose or function is producing a particular, identified individual's likeness or voice without authorisation.

queue.claim: Illinois BIPA treats a 'scan of face geometry' as a biometric identifier, with damages of $1,000 negligent / $5,000 reckless per violation and destruction within 3 years. SB 2979 (2024) made repeat collection from one person a single violation. Zellmer v. Meta (9th Cir. 2024) excluded face data that cannot identify a person.
